Your reviews hit all the right notes, not geeking out, not deprecating a base user.

Bravo! Finally someone said what I have been saying for a long time. For me at a certain level it's not about the processors as the M3 and M4 can handle most anything.But why oh why can't I have a better screen on the Air even if I have to pay extra as an option??? Also my pet peeve as a storage developer for a lot of years is why can't they just leave the 3rd Thunderbolt port in the Air. Sometimes it's just about connectivity and not just ripping performance. I'm also not wanting the extra port to connect yet more displays for crying out loud. 
I appreciate the great videos you have done over the years and hope you continue providing a calm voice in an environment that can become a bit screechy at times.

My 2022 MacBook Air M2 with 16GB handles LogicPro multitrack recording over Dante VSC, occasional Photoshop, regular Premier Pro all while having at least a dozen browser tabs and half a dozen CLI tabs and Thunderbird without a problem.   I wish I had gotten more disk space but boy is it pricey.   I might consider M4 Air with 16GB and at least 500GB SSD only because I need the disk space...

I'm on a beefed out M2 MacBook Pro and I'm still impressed with how amazing ARM technology is. My laptop is so good, the only way I see it ever leaving me is if I outlast the final wave of software support for it, cause it isn't even dipping in speed after a few years like Mac Laptops have been known to do. Like my 2011 MacBook Pro became extremely slow and hence getting my 2016 version. The hardware on the 2016 was fine enough (a little slow, but it could handle 20-30 audio tracks in Logic Pro X), but I had so many battery cycles with this thing, that it only works plugged into the wall. The only hardware from Apple I am interested in is a Mac Studio, because it feels like Apple has FINALLY released a good desktop experience that gets rid of my need for an upgraded laptop. 

Apple hardware has gotten so good, that now people are upgrading not because they need to, but because they want to. That just wasn't the case years back when 2-4 cores was the standard, where there was a good reason to need a better processor and more RAM. Like I love Windows and Linux and x86 hardware, but sheesh, Apple continues to impress me with every year.

I have used Dell Latitude and XPS, and Lenovo Thinkpads in the past. Last year I started using a Macbook M3 at work and was shocked at how fast and efficient it was. I use it for running often 5+ instances of VSCode, docker containers, many dozens of Chrome tabs, Slack, Spotify, 1-2 2k/4k external monitors, and it never even gets warm much less turns the fans on. I bought the Macbook Air M4 with the 512GB storage upgrade last week for personal use and I think it is the best laptop I've ever owned, and is significantly cheaper than the last XPS and the last Thinkpad I got. With these Apple chipsets and unified memory and such excellent passive cooling (or chips that don't get that hot to begin with under most workloads), Apple has so massively surpassed the PC market and Intel/AMD CPUs for the majority of users.
